payload.title: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows
payload.description: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows in go-fsfix by running gomion repo setup, committing the result, and confirming the first Actions runs show no warnings or notices
payload.plan:
# Plan: adopt gomion's generated workflows in go-fsfix

1. Use a gomion build that includes E-2454's `gomion repo` commands.
2. In go-fsfix, run `gomion repo setup`. It raises each go.mod below Go 1.27 and tidies it, then writes .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml.
3. Run `gomion repo setup --check`; it must report the repo up to date.
4. Run each module's tests locally with GOWORK=off.
5. Commit the generated workflows and the raised go.mod/go.sum files together.

After the land: push, then read the annotations on the first Test run (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` for each job), and on the next Release run once there is one. Each must show zero warnings and zero notices; any that remain are fixed in gomion's templates, not here.

ops.statement: go-fsfix's .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml are exactly what gomion repo workflows generates, and gomion repo setup --check reports the repo up to date
Every go.mod in go-fsfix declares go 1.27 or later and is tidy
Does not hand-edit the generated workflow files; a change goes into gomion's templates
After the push, the first Test run and the next Release run show zero Actions warnings and zero notices

payload.title: Prepare go-fsfix for a tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-fsfix for release by committing and pushing pending work, then propose a version and description per module for the owner to tag.
payload.plan:
## Plan
1. Run `git status` and `git log <latest-tag>..HEAD` in the go-fsfix repo; list every module in it that has its own go.mod and tag prefix.
2. Commit any uncommitted work that belongs in the release. Ask the owner about anything unclear instead of guessing.
3. Run the repo's build, vet and tests. Fix or report any failure.
4. Push main to origin. Do not create or push tags.
5. For each module, compare the changes since its latest tag and propose a semver version, explaining whether the change is breaking.
6. Draft a release description for each module.
7. Report the proposed versions and descriptions to the owner. The owner tags and releases when ready.

payload.title: Decide how go-fsfix creates real git repository fixtures
payload.description: Decide how go-fsfix fixtures create real git repositories with files committed, and how that composes with its existing dir and file fixtures
payload.context: Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. payload.description: Add a GoModFixture that embeds RepoFixture and declares a Go module's go.mod (module path, go version, requires, replaces) so tests get a committed repo with a generated go.mod without hand-writing its text.

fields.context:
Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. gomion's gompkg tests shell out to git directly (init, add, commit with fixed author env) from a test file; gomion also has its own gommod/gitutils package. Mike: git belongs in go-gitutil. Needed first by go-fsfix real repo fixtures and by gomion tests; mocking git is ruled out because it misses edge cases such as permissions.

Scope added from the go-fsfix brainstorm E-2547 (settled with Mike on 2026-11-06; its outcome holds the design). go-fsfix's RepoFixture now always creates a real repository and gains AddClone and AddWorktree, so the fixture operations go-gitutil must offer are: init with a branch name, forced add of every file, commit with a message and ident, clone, and worktree-add on a new branch. Ident is dt.Mailbox (a Name plus a dt.EmailAddress), which go-dt gains in a task filed from E-2547; go-gitutil defines no identity type of its own and names the field or parameter Ident. The add operation sets advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false so a fixture repo nested in another is recorded as an embedded repository without git's advice message. go-fsfix keeps the *Repo it used and returns it from RepoFixture.Repo(), so init must hand back a usable Repo without a second rev-parse.

Raised by Mike on 2026-11-03 in the E-2546 brainstorm. gompkg's repo setup test has a three-line goModFile(modPath, goVersion) helper that concatenates a go.mod body; the plain go.mod tree fixtures in replace_management, require_check, gogit module_scope and the test module do similar by hand. Mike: this should be standardised in an external package extracted from gommod/goutils rather than live in go-fsfix, which is filesystem-generic and should not know Go. Building on modfile lets the same package emit require and replace lines for fixtures that exercise replace management.

Open question added from the go-fsfix brainstorm E-2547 on 2026-11-06: does a module path earn a go-dt type (dt.ModulePath), or does it stay here? Mike's position: Go-related types are admissible in go-dt (Go's own stdlib carries Go AST types), but a module path may not differ enough from a DirPath to earn one. The differences: for `go get` to fetch it, the first element must contain a dot because it is read as a host (`github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt` fetches; `myorg/mylib` fails with "malformed module path: missing dot in first path element"; stdlib paths such as `net/http` are the deliberate exception), and a major version 2 or higher must appear as a `/vN` suffix that matches the tag (`github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt/v2` with tag v2.0.0; `/v1` and `/v0` are invalid). go-dt has no dependencies, so a dt.ModulePath would validate by hand rather than through x/mod's module.CheckPath. GoModFixture (E-2564) in go-fsfix consumes whatever this task produces.

payload.title: Fixtures live in go-fsfix and depend on production packages, never the reverse
payload.description: A fixture is test code. When a fixture needs knowledge a production package owns (go.mod handling, git operations), go-fsfix imports that package; the production package carries no fixture or other test helper. Test code pulling a dependency is the cheap direction; production code carrying test code is not. Mike stated this in the E-2547 brainstorm on 2026-11-06 when placing GoModFixture, reversing the plan's placement beside the go.mod code. It does not mean go-fsfix integrates every sibling: go-fsfix stays out of go-cfgstore for now because the integration saved no lines.

payload.title: Make RepoFixture create a real git repository
payload.description: Make every RepoFixture init, add and commit its declared files through go-gitutil, add AddClone, AddWorktree, Repo(), AddFiles and Reconcile, and export the branch, message and author defaults.
payload.context: Designed in the E-2547 brainstorm with Mike, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-06; the full synthesis is E-2547's outcome. gomion (E-2540, E-2559) needs fixtures that are real git repositories with files committed: git rev-parse must work, then a test adds an untracked file or modifies a committed one before running the code under test. RepoFixture today only makes an empty .git directory (repo_fixture.go createWithParent). Git operations come from go-gitutil (E-2548 decides their shape); the identity type comes from go-dt (E-2567). go-fsfix must not shell out to git itself.
payload.analysis:
# Design settled in E-2547

## RepoFixture always creates a real repository
- No opt-in flag and no NoGit escape. A test that wants only a `.git` marker builds a DirFixture with a `.git` DirFixture child.
- Creation order stays directory, declared files, children; then one git step: init with branch, forced add of every file, one commit. Every declared file is committed; ignore rules cannot drop one.
- After Create the repo is clean with exactly one commit. A test wanting untracked or modified files makes them after Create (see Reconcile) and further commits through Repo().
- RepoFixture nested inside a RepoFixture is allowed. The inner repo commits first (walk order); the outer forced add records it as an embedded repository (a gitlink). go-gitutil's add sets advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false. A proper AddSubmodule with .gitmodules waits until a test needs it.

## Args are flat (Mike's principle)
    type RepoFixtureArgs struct {
        Files        []*FileFixture
        Permissions  int
        ModifiedTime time.Time
        Branch       string      // "" means DefaultBranch
        Message      string      // "" means DefaultCommitMessage
        Author       dt.Mailbox  // zero means DefaultAuthor
        Committer    dt.Mailbox  // zero means Author
    }

## Exported defaults, composed
    const (
        DefaultBranch        = "main"
        DefaultCommitMessage = "fsfix: initial commit"
        DefaultAuthorName    = "go-fsfix"
        DefaultAuthorEmail   dt.EmailAddress = "fsfix@example.com"
    )
    var DefaultAuthor = dt.NewMailbox(DefaultAuthorName, DefaultAuthorEmail)

## Repo accessor
- RepoFixture keeps the *gitutil.Repo it used and returns it from `Repo()`, guarded by ensureCreated. go-gitutil is already in the consumer's build, so the accessor adds no dependency.

## AddClone and AddWorktree
- `origin.AddClone(t, name, args) *RepoFixture`: a clone is a sibling of the origin on disk (a clone inside the working tree would be an embedded repo). Implementation appends the clone to the origin's parent's ChildFixtures; since children create in order and the origin was added first, the clone runs after the origin's commit with no special ordering code.
- `repo.AddWorktree(t, name, &WorktreeFixtureArgs{Branch}) *WorktreeFixture`: same sibling placement; a linked worktree has a `.git` file rather than a directory, so it is its own small type.
- Both delegate to go-gitutil's clone and worktree-add.

## AddFiles map form
- `AddFiles(t, map[dt.RelFilepath]string)` on RootFixture, DirFixture and RepoFixture, beside AddFileFixtures. Keys are file paths; directories come from the keys (createFile already runs MkdirAll). An empty directory still needs AddDirFixture. Builder calls stay for permissions, times and ContentFunc.

## Reconcile instead of new write verbs
- `Reconcile(t)` on RootFixture (and the other fixtures) walks the tree and rewrites every declared file so disk matches the declaration: missing files appear, modified ones revert, declarations added after Create get created. Useful at the top of a loop iteration.
- Reconcile never commits. Git state is set once at Create, so a file added after Create is untracked and a committed file rewritten after Create shows as modified, the two states gomion's tests need.
- The silent case today (AddFileFixture after Create appends to FileFixtures but writes nothing, dir_fixture.go) is resolved by Reconcile, not by a fatal.

## Dependency and release
- go-fsfix requires the whole go-gitutil module; x/mod comes with it. go directive rises to 1.27.0; go-dt to the release that has E-2567.
- Release order: go-dt (E-2567), go-gitutil (E-2548's implementation, no replace directives), then go-fsfix. Local development uses go.work.

## Tests and docs
- go-fsfix's test module verifies through go-gitutil's read side (branch, log, status) plus one assertion needing no git: GitPath() contains HEAD and objects. No git invocation from a test file.
- README gains a real-repo section, documents Create versus Reconcile, and drops the "simulate" wording.

## Not in this task
- GoModFixture: E-2564. go-cfgstore integration: none (zero lines saved). AddSubmodule: when needed.

fields.outcome:
# Synthesis: how go-fsfix creates real git repository fixtures

Brainstorm with Mike, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-06. The plan on this task listed eight open questions; the conversation answered all eight and reshaped several of them. Everything below is Mike's call unless marked as accepted on my advice.

## Decisions Mike made

1. **RepoFixture always creates a real repository.** No opt-in flag, no NoGit escape. Mike's reasoning: no test calls AddRepoFixture without wanting a repository, and a NoGit RepoFixture is just a DirFixture. A test that wants only a `.git` marker nests a `.git` DirFixture in a DirFixture. The plan's Q1 (nested GitArgs pointer, flat bool, separate constructor, NoGit) is moot.

2. **Args stay flat.** Mike's principle: `*Args` structs hold fields, not nested option objects. `RepoFixtureArgs` gains `Branch`, `Message`, `Author` and `Committer` beside its existing fields. Branch and message are facts about the repo that the call adding it configures.

3. **The identity type is `dt.Mailbox` in go-dt, not a go-gitutil-local type.** The plan had coined "Identity"; Mike rejected a package-local type with a generic name and chose the third option: name what the thing is and put it in go-dt for every package to share. It is RFC 5322's mailbox, a display name plus an email address. Mike chose a struct over a string because a mailbox has two distinct values, and chose `dt.EmailAddress` as its own type because an email address is a subset of string, so a function can take one and either validate it or rightly assume it is valid. Constructor `NewMailbox`, parsers `ParseMailbox` and `ParseEmailAddress`, accessors `LocalPart()` and `Domain()` on EmailAddress (LocalPart, not Name, so it does not collide with Mailbox.Name). net/mail's Address is not used directly because its String() renders RFC 5322 quoting and RFC 2047 encoding, which git would store literally; net/mail remains the parser. go-gitutil names its field or parameter `Ident`, of type `dt.Mailbox`.

4. **Defaults are exported constants, composed.** `DefaultBranch`, `DefaultCommitMessage`, `DefaultAuthorName`, `DefaultAuthorEmail`, and `var DefaultAuthor = dt.NewMailbox(DefaultAuthorName, DefaultAuthorEmail)`. A test overrides any of them through the args.

5. **`RepoFixture.Repo()` returns the `*gitutil.Repo` go-fsfix used.** Mike accepted option A once the cost was reduced to one accessor: with Mailbox in go-dt, the return type of `Repo()` is the only go-gitutil type in go-fsfix's exported API, and go-gitutil is already in every consumer's build.

6. **`AddClone` and `AddWorktree` on RepoFixture, delegating to go-gitutil.** Mike proposed them; they replace the plan's "three sibling DirFixtures and the test calls go-gitutil". A clone or worktree is a sibling of its source on disk (inside the working tree it would be an embedded repository). Appending it to the source's parent gives the right creation order for free since children create in the order added. A linked worktree has a `.git` file, not a directory, so it gets its own `WorktreeFixture` type. This grows E-2548's scope to clone and worktree-add; recorded in E-2548's context.

7. **Nested RepoFixtures are allowed, not refused.** Mike asked what refusing would buy; nothing, once the walk order is considered: the inner repo commits first, and the outer forced add records it as an embedded repository (a gitlink, a submodule minus `.gitmodules`). go-gitutil's add sets `advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false`. A proper `AddSubmodule` waits until a test needs one; Mike avoids submodules but expects to meet repos that use them.

8. **`Reconcile` instead of new write verbs.** Mike proposed it in place of the plan's `WriteFile`/`Write` and the late-`AddFileFixture` fatal. `Reconcile(t)` walks the tree and rewrites every declared file so disk matches the declaration: missing files appear, modified ones revert, declarations added after Create get created. It can run at the top of a loop iteration. It never commits, so a file added after Create is untracked and a committed file rewritten after Create shows as modified, the two states gomion's tests need. Per ED-1550 this is part of the one implementation task, not a separate mutation task.

9. **GoModFixture lives in go-fsfix, not beside the go.mod code.** Mike reversed the plan's placement: a fixture is test code, go-goutil (E-2557's extraction) is production code and should carry no test helpers, and test code pulling a dependency is the cheap direction. Recorded as decision ED-1651 (proposed) and filed as E-2564, blocked by E-2557 and E-2568. Whether any part of a go.mod description earns a go-dt type is E-2557's question; Mike doubts `ModulePath` since its values are DirPath-shaped. The two rules that distinguish a module path (dot in the first element for fetchability, `/vN` suffix matching the major version) are recorded in E-2557's context.

10. **go-fsfix does not integrate go-cfgstore, for now.** Mike had been open to it and noted go-fsfix may import go-cfgstore even though go-cfgstore's test module imports go-fsfix. Convinced by the arithmetic: the integrated form saves zero lines over a DirFixture plus go-cfgstore's own DirsProvider helper. Revisit if a richer case appears (seeded config files in layout).

11. **The release chain is accepted:** go-dt (E-2567), then go-gitutil (E-2548's implementation, with its replace directives gone and go-diffutils tagged), then go-fsfix (E-2568), then gomion. Mike: deliberating over ordering costs more than using blocks and doing it; streamlining chained landings is filed elsewhere. Local development uses go.work, so only tagging is serial.

## Accepted on my advice

- **Every declared file is committed in one commit at Create.** Mike accepted without claiming to understand the ramifications; they are: the repo is clean after Create with one commit; a test needing untracked or modified files makes them after Create via AddFileFixture plus Reconcile; the add is forced so a declared file an ignore rule would skip is tracked anyway; further commits go through `Repo()`. The alternative, a per-file `Uncommitted` flag, can be added later if a test wants a mixed starting state in one declaration.
- **go-fsfix requires the whole go-gitutil module** rather than asking E-2548 for a nested module. x/mod comes with it and is wanted for E-2564 anyway.
- **go-fsfix's own tests verify through go-gitutil's read side** (branch, log, status) plus one assertion needing no git: `GitPath()` contains HEAD and objects. No git invocation from a test file.
- **`AddFiles(t, map[dt.RelFilepath]string)`** as a method beside the builder calls, on RootFixture, DirFixture and RepoFixture. Keys are file paths; directories come from the keys.

## Things that stay out
- go-fsfix never shells out to git itself and learns nothing about go.mod generation or go-cfgstore layouts.
- E-2548 does not block this brainstorm; it blocks E-2568.

## Follow-ups spawned
- E-2567 (go-dt): Add EmailAddress and Mailbox types. Cleans up E-2547.
- E-2568 (go-fsfix): Make RepoFixture create a real git repository. The design above is its analysis. Blocked by E-2567 and E-2548; blocks E-2540 and E-2559; cleans up E-2547. When E-2548 spawns its implementation task, re-point E-2568's blocked-by at that task.
- E-2564 (go-fsfix): Add GoModFixture. Blocked by E-2557 and E-2568; cleans up E-2547; implements ED-1651.
- ED-1651 (proposed): Fixtures live in go-fsfix and depend on production packages, never the reverse.
- E-2548's context now carries the enlarged scope (init with branch, forced add-all, commit with Ident, clone, worktree-add, advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false, Repo usable from init).
- E-2557's context now carries the ModulePath question with examples.

payload.reason: Overly broad and could be read as moving production code. Mike's argument was narrower: go-fsfix integrates git because git fixtures are widely used; functionality most users do not need (his example: Oracle DB) does not belong in go-fsfix just because a fixture could use it.

# Design settled in E-2547

## RepoFixture always creates a real repository
- No opt-in flag and no NoGit escape. A test that wants only a `.git` marker builds a DirFixture with a `.git` DirFixture child.
- Creation order stays directory, declared files, children; then one git step: init with branch, forced add of every file, one commit. Every declared file is committed; ignore rules cannot drop one.
- After Create the repo is clean with exactly one commit. A test wanting untracked or modified files makes them after Create (see Reconcile) and further commits through Repo().
- RepoFixture nested inside a RepoFixture is allowed. The inner repo commits first (walk order); the outer forced add records it as an embedded repository (a gitlink). go-gitutil's add sets advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false. A proper AddSubmodule with .gitmodules waits until a test needs it.

## Args are flat (Mike's principle)
    type RepoFixtureArgs struct {
        Files        []*FileFixture
        Permissions  int
        ModifiedTime time.Time
        Branch       dt.GitBranchName // "" means DefaultBranch
        Message      string           // "" means DefaultCommitMessage
        Author       dt.Mailbox       // zero means DefaultAuthor
        Committer    dt.Mailbox       // zero means Author
        CommitTime   time.Time        // zero means DefaultCommitTime
    }

## Exported defaults, composed
    const (
        DefaultBranch        dt.GitBranchName    = "main"
        DefaultCommitMessage                     = "fsfix: initial commit"
        DefaultAuthorName    dt.EmailDisplayName = "go-fsfix"
        DefaultAuthorEmail   dt.EmailAddress     = "fsfix@example.com"
    )
    var DefaultAuthor = dt.Mailbox{DisplayName: DefaultAuthorName, Email: DefaultAuthorEmail} // go-dt has no NewMailbox (E-2567)
    var DefaultCommitTime = time.Date(2000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

## Repo accessor
- RepoFixture keeps the *gitutil.Repo it used and returns it from `Repo()`, guarded by ensureCreated. go-gitutil is already in the consumer's build, so the accessor adds no dependency.

## AddClone and AddWorktree
- `origin.AddClone(t, name, args) *RepoFixture`: a clone is a sibling of the origin on disk (a clone inside the working tree would be an embedded repo). Implementation appends the clone to the origin's parent's ChildFixtures; since children create in order and the origin was added first, the clone runs after the origin's commit with no special ordering code.
- `repo.AddWorktree(t, name, &WorktreeFixtureArgs{Branch}) *WorktreeFixture`: same sibling placement; a linked worktree has a `.git` file rather than a directory, so it is its own small type.
- Both delegate to go-gitutil's clone and worktree-add.

## AddFiles map form
- `AddFiles(t, map[dt.RelFilepath]string)` on RootFixture, DirFixture and RepoFixture, beside AddFileFixtures. Keys are file paths; directories come from the keys (createFile already runs MkdirAll). An empty directory still needs AddDirFixture. Builder calls stay for permissions, times and ContentFunc.

## Reconcile instead of new write verbs
- Mike proposed it in E-2547: "maybe we need a Reconcile() method ... that can be called later to fixup anything still needing fixed up, or even called before each iteration of a loop during testing?"
- `Reconcile(t)` on RootFixture (and the other fixtures) walks the tree and rewrites every declared file so disk matches the declaration: missing files appear, modified ones revert, declarations added after Create get created.
- Reconcile never commits and never runs git. Git state is set once at Create, so a file added after Create is untracked and a committed file rewritten after Create shows as modified, the two states gomion's tests need.
- The silent case today (AddFileFixture after Create appends to FileFixtures but writes nothing, dir_fixture.go) is resolved by Reconcile, not by a fatal.

## Dependency and release
- go-fsfix requires the whole go-gitutil module; x/mod comes with it. go directive rises to 1.27.0; go-dt to the release that has E-2567 and E-2599.
- Release order: go-dt (E-2567, E-2599), go-gitutil (E-2600, no replace directives), then go-fsfix. Local development uses go.work.

## Tests and docs
- go-fsfix's test module verifies through go-gitutil's read side (branch, log, status) plus one assertion needing no git: GitPath() contains HEAD and objects. No git invocation from a test file.
- README gains a real-repo section, documents Create versus Reconcile, and drops the "simulate" wording.

# Decided while planning (2026-11-12, with Mike)

## Fixture git ignores the machine's git config (Mike: C)
- A machine's global or system config can change or break fixture commits: `commit.gpgsign=true` tries to sign (fails or prompts without a key or agent), `core.hooksPath` runs global hooks, `core.autocrlf` rewrites line endings, `init.templateDir` copies hooks into each new repo.
- Fixture creation runs git with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the same declaration gives the same repo on every machine.
- The fixture repo's own config also gets `commit.gpgsign=false`, an empty `core.hooksPath` and `core.autocrlf=false`, so code under test that commits inside a fixture behaves the same on every machine too. Cost accepted: a test of config-reading behaviour sees those entries.
- Rejected: inheriting the machine's config (fixtures differ by machine); isolating creation only (code under test still hits the machine's signing and hooks).

## Commit dates are fixed (Mike: B)
- `DefaultCommitTime`, overridable by `RepoFixtureArgs.CommitTime`, applied as both author and committer date. The same declaration gives the same commit hash everywhere, so tests can assert hashes and keep golden output.
- Cost accepted: code under test that compares commit age to now sees an old commit unless the test sets CommitTime.
- Rejected: the current time (hashes change per run); reusing ModifiedTime (it already means the directory's file time).

## Reconcile can remove undeclared files, opt-in (Mike: C)
- `ReconcileArgs.RemoveUndeclared` deletes files on disk that no FileFixture declares, never touching `.git` or a nested repo's `.git`. Without it, Reconcile deletes nothing, so files a test wrote directly stay for inspection.
- Rejected: never removing (an iteration inherits the previous one's leftovers); always removing (deletes files a test wrote on purpose).

## A clean git state comes from recreating, not from reset (Mike: B)
- My first framing of this question offered only "disk only" or "reset and checkout inside Reconcile"; it omitted wipe-and-recreate. Mike noted tests should not depend on a prior test's state and asked whether recreating could take seconds.
- Measured on git 2.52 with global and system config isolated, init + forced add + commit: 41 ms for 10 files, 59 ms for 100, 95 ms for 1,000, 412 ms for 10,000. A loop pays this per iteration; reset plus checkout would also start git processes, so the saving for small fixtures is about half, not an order of magnitude. Windows process start is slower and unmeasured; it scales both alike.
- Mike: "If no, then B definitely." So a test needing a clean git state calls Cleanup and then Create again (a new temp directory, a fresh repo), or builds a fixture per iteration. Recreation restores everything (branches, tags, worktrees, untracked files), which reset and checkout would not, and go-gitutil needs no reset or checkout for fixtures.

## Branch type is dt.GitBranchName (Mike)
- go-gitutil's GitRef is used where git means a revision, broader than a branch name (`HEAD~1`, `refs/tags/v1`). Mike asked for git's concepts to be fully modelled and reused across packages, in go-dt's root package, each name prefixed with Git: E-2599 (GitRefName, GitBranchName, GitTagName, GitRemoteName, GitRevision, GitObjectID). A second domain-types package was rejected because developers would have to discover it and choose between it and go-dt.
- WorktreeFixtureArgs.Branch and CloneFixtureArgs.Branch use the same type.

## Decided without asking (Mike could object; none did)
- `AddClone` takes its own `CloneFixtureArgs` (Branch to check out, Permissions, ModifiedTime). RepoFixtureArgs' Files, Message, Author, Committer and CommitTime mean nothing for a clone.
- A missing git binary fails the test (`t.Fatal`), never skips it; a skipped suite can pass while testing nothing. Mike confirmed (Q7: A).
- A worktree's branch defaults to the fixture's name, matching `git worktree add <path>`.
- A git failure during Create calls `t.Fatal`: later steps depend on it.
- Author and Committer stay separate; git sets both through environment variables or the `author.*`/`committer.*` config keys.
- Items state behaviour; go-gitutil's call names come from E-2600.
